name.description: The name of the service/resource this status is for.

message.description: Additional detail, such as error/warning message.

timestamp.description: The instant at which the status changed last.

title:
Any type that implements validation of service or resource status can be published as a "health check" by mixing
in this type. These can be queried programmatically or monitored through the Console.

Each instance of the HealthCheck type represents the status of a single identifiable service or resource.
UIs should call {@link HealthCheck#poll} to get all the status values for display.

There should be a type for each logical category of services/resources, identified by the name of the sub type.
Within each instance of that type of HealthCheck, the name identifies the specific resource. If the name is null,
there must be only a single instance of that type.

For example, DatastoreHealthCheck might produce these values:
```json
[
  {
     "type": "DatastoreHealthCheck",
     "name": "PostgreSQL",
     "status": "WARNING",
     "message": "Vacuum needed on table C3_2_IMPRTNT_STUFF",
     "timestamp": "2019-04-30T12:30:45.055Z"
  },
  {
     "type": "DatastoreHealthCheck",
     "name": "Cassandra",
     "status": "OK",
     "message": "All 12 nodes up",
     "timestamp": "2019-04-30T12:30:45.056Z"
  }
]
```

This should be displayed to the user as something like:
```
⚠  Datastore (PostgreSQL)  Vacuum needed on table C3_2_IMPRTNT_STUFF
✔  Datastore (Cassandra)   All 12 nodes up
```
Note that "Datastore" comes from the name of the type of the results and the specific database is in the name.

@see https://status.aws.amazon.com/
